en: The Sūtra on the Measurement of the Merits of All Buddha-fields,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court-Scattered Grandee, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments,
Great Master of Illuminating Teaching, the Subject Faxian, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard:

At one time the Buddha was at the Bodhimaṇḍa in the Dharma-field of Rājagṛha, seated upon a lion throne of vajra-maṇi jewels, surrounded on all sides by a multitude of bodhisattva-mahāsattvas; furthermore, there were hundreds of thousands of koṭis of nayutas of beings from ten buddha-fields listening to the Buddha’s teaching of the Dharma.

At that time, there was a bodhisattva mahāsattva in the assembly named King of Inconceivable Light. He rose from his seat, surveyed the great assembly of bodhisattvas, and addressed the multitude, saying:
"O sons of the Buddha, you should now listen attentively!
The duration of one full great kalpa in this Sahā world, when measured by time, constitutes a single day and night in that Western Land of Utmost Bliss, the realm of the Buddha Amitāyus.
“O Son of the Buddha!
One great kalpa of that world of Sukhāvatī, when measured by its duration, constitutes a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Vajrasagarapramardin of the world Animiṣā.”
“O Son of the Buddha!

One great kalpa in that world Animiṣā, when measured by its duration, constitutes a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Padmottara-deha within the world-system Avivartyacakra-prabhā.”
“O Son of the Buddha!

One great eon in the world-system Radiance of the Non-retrogressive Wheel is equal in duration to a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Dharma King within the world-system Free from Dust.”
“O Son of the Buddha!
One great kalpa in that World Without Dust, when measured by its duration, is but a single day and night within the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Siṃha in the World of Lamp Light.”
“O Son of the Buddha!
One great eon in the world-system of Lamp-Light, when measured by its duration, constitutes a single day and night within the buddha-field of Vairocana Tathāgata in the world-system of Good Light.”
“O Son of the Buddha!
One great kalpa in that world of Good Light, when measured by its duration, constitutes a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Dharmavyūhadeha in the world Difficult to Conquer.”
“O Son of the Buddha!

One great eon (*mahākalpa*) in that world Difficult to Conquer, when measured by its duration, constitutes a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Universal King of All-Penetrating Mind in the world Mūha.”
“O Son of the Buddha!
One great kalpa in that world Mūha, when measured by its duration, constitutes a single day and night in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Praśastaprabha in the world Abhimukhaprabhā.”
“O Son of the Buddha!

In this way, after a number of eons equal to the calculation of kalpas exceeding the dust motes of ten hundred-thousand koṭi-nayuta buddha-fields, there is a world named Padmaśrī; the World-Honored Buddha there is named Bhadraśrī, and this constitutes one day and night within that buddha-field.”
“O Son of the Buddha!
There is a bodhisattva stage called the Stage of Universal Practice (*samantacaryā-bhūmi*), in which one performs such immeasurable bodhisattva practices.
O Son of the Buddha!”

Furthermore, if there should be a person who receives, upholds, reads, recites, and explains to others this *Sarvabuddhakṣetraguṇavyūhasaṃsūcana-sūtra*, at the time of that person’s death, all the Tathāgatas of the Buddhas in Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions will appear before them, fulfilling every one of that sentient being’s aspirations.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, the Bodhisattva King of Inconceivable Radiance and the great assembly, having heard what the Buddha taught, were all greatly rejoiced; they believed, accepted, and practiced it accordingly.
The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on Measuring the Merits of All Buddha-fields.
